correctness.rationale: The all-length derivation uses the Rule-45 Boolean identity, a justified cyclic closure by propagation contradiction, finite injectivity-to-surjectivity, an exact squarefree monomial count and conditional balancing of each Boolean derivative. Independent forward-table and inverse-formula comparisons for all outputs of odd lengths 1..15, full influence counts for 64 site coordinates, and ANF-support Möbius checks through 13 all passed (VERIFY_OK). claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An arbitrary bijection can have arbitrary ANF and arbitrary directional influence distribution. Preimage counts therefore do not imply the exact sensitivity spectrum, while n=3 finite inversion does not establish the infinitely parameterized polynomial or sharp radius. The present proof makes independent calculations.

originality.rationale: Odd-ring bijectivity itself is previously proved (Hudcová, Theorem 28) and is not novel. Neither her direct Rule-45 preimage-count classification nor the 2022 inverse-rule discussion at lengths 1 and 3 states the sparse all-odd-length inverse ANF, exact directional influence law or its sharp inverse-radius consequence. The 1984 paper's nonlinear example is Rule 18 and its principal exact classification is additive. Published record search and accessible prior claims found no stronger equivalent coverage, with qualified historical priority.
residual_risks: An older, differently named Boolean-network inverse circuit or an unindexed Rule-45 symmetry-equivalent formula might already imply the ANF or sensitivity law.
Some figure pages in the larger original reports were not directly inspected; relevant full-text arguments and statements were inspected.

value.rationale: Exact inversion architecture and sitewise differential sensitivity are intrinsic, usable invariants of a naturally reversible (odd finite-ring) nonlinear cellular automaton. The result distinguishes globally essential dependence (sharp radius (n-1)/2) from strong anisotropic mean-case influence with a geometric law and a sparse O(n) inverse Boolean circuit. The motivation does not rest on merely rephrasing prior odd-ring bijectivity or a small finite experiment.
